e\fR searches for \fBage\-plugin\-example\fR in the PATH and executes it to perform the file header encryption or decryption\. The plugin may request input from the user through \fBage\fR to complete the operation\.
.P
Plugins can be freely mixed with other plugins or natively supported keys\.
.P
A plugin is not bound to only encrypt or decrypt files meant for or generated by the plugin\. For example, a plugin can be used to decrypt files encrypted to a native X25519 \fBRECIPIENT\fR or even with a passphrase\. Similarly, a plugin can encrypt a file such that it can be decrypted without the use of any plugin\.
.P
Plugins for which the \fBIDENTITY\fR/\fBRECIPIENT\fR distinction doesn't make sense (such as a symmetric encryption plugin) may generate only an \fBIDENTITY\fR and instruct the user to perform encryption with the \fB\-e\fR/\fB\-\-encrypt\fR and \fB\-i\fR/\fB\-\-identity\fR flags\. Plugins for which the concept of separate identities doesn't make sense (such as a password\-encryption plugin) may instruct the user to use the \fB\-j\fR flag\.
.P
\fBage\fR can natively encrypt to recipients starting with \fBage1tag1\fR (using P\-256 ECDH) or \fBage1tagpq1\fR (using the ML\-KEM\-768 + P\-256 post\-quantum hybrid)\. These are intended to be the public side of private keys held in hardware\.
.P
They are directly supported to avoid the need to install the plugin, which may be platform\-specific, on the encrypting side\.
.P
The tag reduces privacy, by allowing an observer to correlate files with a recipient (but not files amongst them without knowledge of the recipient), but this is also a desirable property for hardware keys that require user interaction for each decryption operation\.

\fBage\fR will exit 0 if and only if encryption or decryption are successful for the full length of the input\.

Support for post-quantum keys is built into age v1.3.0 and later. Alternatively,
the `age-plugin-pq` binary can be installed and placed in `$PATH` to add support
to any version and implementation of age that supports plugins. Recipients will
work out of the box, while identities will have to be converted to plugin
identities with `age-plugin-pq -identity`.

### Passphrases

Files can be encrypted with a passphrase by using `-p/--passphrase`. By default age will automatically generate a secure passphrase. Passphrase protected files are automatically detected at decrypt time.

```
$ age -p secrets.txt > secrets.txt.age
Enter passphrase (leave empty to autogenerate a secure one):
Using the autogenerated passphrase "release-response-step-brand-wrap-ankle-pair-unusual-sword-train".
$ age -d secrets.txt.age > secrets.txt
Enter passphrase:
```

### Passphrase-protected key files

If an identity file passed to `-i` is a passphrase encrypted age file, it will be automatically decrypted.

```
$ age-keygen | age -p > key.age
Public key: age1yhm4gctwfmrpz87tdslm550wrx6m79y9f2hdzt0lndjnehwj0ukqrjpyx5
Enter passphrase (leave empty to autogenerate a secure one):
Using the autogenerated passphrase "hip-roast-boring-snake-mention-east-wasp-honey-input-actress".
$ age -r age1yhm4gctwfmrpz87tdslm550wrx6m79y9f2hdzt0lndjnehwj0ukqrjpyx5 secrets.txt > secrets.txt.age
$ age -d -i key.age secrets.txt.age > secrets.txt
Enter passphrase for identity file "key.age":
```

Passphrase-protected identity files are not necessary for most use cases, where access to the encrypted identity file implies access to the whole system. However, they can be useful if the identity file is stored remotely.

### SSH keys

As a convenience feature, age also supports encrypting to `ssh-rsa` and `ssh-ed25519` SSH public keys, and decrypting with the respective private key file. (`ssh-agent` is not supported.)

```
$ age -R ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub example.jpg > example.jpg.age
$ age -d -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 example.jpg.age > example.jpg
```

Note that SSH key support employs more complex cryptography, and embeds a public key tag in the encrypted file, making it possible to track files that are encrypted to a specific public key.

#### Encrypting to a GitHub user

Combining SSH key support and `-R`, you can easily encrypt a file to the SSH keys listed on a GitHub profile.

```
$ curl https://github.com/benjojo.keys | age -R - example.jpg > example.jpg.age
```

Keep in mind that people might not protect SSH keys long-term, since they are revokable when used only for authentication, and that SSH keys held on YubiKeys can't be used to decrypt files.

### Inspecting encrypted files

The `age-inspect` command can display metadata about an encrypted file without decrypting it, including the recipient types, whether it uses post-quantum encryption, and the payload size.

```
$ age-inspect secrets.age
secrets.age is an age file, version "age-encryption.org/v1".

This file is encrypted to the following recipient types:
  - "mlkem768x25519"

This file uses post-quantum encryption.

Size breakdown (assuming it decrypts successfully):

    Header                      1627 bytes
    Encryption overhead           32 bytes
    Payload                       42 bytes
                        -------------------
    Total                       1701 bytes

```

For scripting, use `--json` to get machine-readable output.

This option can be repeated\. Identities are tried in the order in which are provided, and the first one matching one of the file's recipients is used\. Unused identities are ignored, but it is an error if the \fIINPUT\fR file is passphrase\-encrypted and \fB\-i\fR/\fB\-\-identity\fR is specified\.
.TP
\fB\-j\fR \fIPLUGIN\fR
Decrypt using the data\-less \fIplugin\fR \fIPLUGIN\fR\.
.IP
This is equivalent to using \fB\-i\fR/\fB\-\-identity\fR with a file that contains a single plugin \fBIDENTITY\fR that encodes no plugin\-specific data\.
.SH "RECIPIENTS AND IDENTITIES"
\fBRECIPIENTS\fR are public values, like a public key, that a file can be encrypted to\. \fBIDENTITIES\fR are private values, like a private key, that allow decrypting a file encrypted to the corresponding \fBRECIPIENT\fR\.
.SS "Native keys"
Native \fBage\fR key pairs are generated with age\-keygen(1), and provide small encodings and strong encryption based on X25519 for classic keys, and X25519 + ML\-KEM\-768 for post\-quantum hybrid keys\. The post\-quantum hybrid keys are secure against future quantum computers and are the recommended recipient type for most applications\.
.P
A hybrid \fBRECIPIENT\fR encoding begins with \fBage1pq1\fR and looks like the following:
.IP "" 4
.nf
age1pq167[\|\.\|\.\|\. 1950 more characters \|\.\|\.\|\.]
.fi
.IP "" 0
.P
A hybrid \fBIDENTITY\fR encoding begins with \fBAGE\-SECRET\-KEY\-PQ\-1\fR and looks like the following:
.IP "" 4
.nf
AGE\-SECRET\-KEY\-PQ\-1K30MYPZAHAXHR22YHH27EGDVLU0QNSUH3DSV7J7NR3X6D9LHXNWSDLTV4T
.fi
.IP "" 0
.P
A classic \fBRECIPIENT\fR encoding begins with \fBage1\fR and looks like the following:
.IP "" 4
.nf
age1gde3ncmahlqd9gg50tanl99r960llztrhfapnmx853s4tjum03uqfssgdh
.fi
.IP "" 0
.P
A classic \fBIDENTITY\fR encoding begins with \fBAGE\-SECRET\-KEY\-1\fR and looks like the following:
.IP "" 4
.nf
AGE\-SECRET\-KEY\-1KTYK6RVLN5TAPE7VF6FQQSKZ9HWWCDSKUGXXNUQDWZ7XXT5YK5LSF3UTKQ
.fi
.IP "" 0
.P
A file can't be encrypted to both post\-quantum and classic keys, as that would defeat the post\-quantum security of the encryption\.
.P
An encrypted file can't be linked to the native recipient it's encrypted to without access to the corresponding identity\.
.SS "SSH keys"
As a convenience feature, \fBage\fR also supports encrypting to RSA or Ed25519 ssh(1) keys\. RSA keys must be at least 2048 bits\. This feature employs more complex cryptography, and should only be used when a native key is not available for the recipient\. Note that SSH keys might not be protected long\-term by the recipient, since they are revokable when used only for authentication\.
.P
A \fBRECIPIENT\fR encoding is an SSH public key in \fBauthorized_keys\fR format (see the \fBAUTHORIZED_KEYS FILE FORMAT\fR section of sshd(8)), starting with \fBssh\-rsa\fR or \fBssh\-ed25519\fR, like the following:
.IP "" 4
.nf
ssh\-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAAADAQABAAABgQDULTit0KUehbi[\|\.\|\.\|\.]GU4BtElAbzh8=
ssh\-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIH9pO5pz22JZEas[\|\.\|\.\|\.]l1uZc31FGYMXa
.fi
.IP "" 0
.P
The comment at the end of the line, if present, is ignored\.
.P
In recipient files passed to \fB\-R\fR/\fB\-\-recipients\-file\fR, unsupported but valid SSH public keys are ignored with a warning, to facilitate using \fBauthorized_keys\fR or GitHub \fB\.keys\fR files\. (See \fIEXAMPLES\fR\.)
.P
An \fBIDENTITY\fR is an SSH private key \fIfile\fR passed individually to \fB\-i\fR/\fB\-\-identity\fR\. Note that keys held on hardware tokens such as YubiKeys or accessed via ssh\-agent(1) are not supported\.
.P
An encrypted file \fIcan\fR be linked to the SSH public key it was encrypted to\. This is so that \fBage\fR can identify the correct SSH private key before requesting its password, if any\.
.SS "Plugins"
\fBage\fR can be extended through plugins\. A plugin is only loaded if a corresponding \fBRECIPIENT\fR or \fBIDENTITY\fR is specified\. (Simply decrypting a file encrypted with a plugin will not cause it to load, for security reasons among others\.)
.P
A \fBRECIPIENT\fR for a plugin named \fBexample\fR starts with \fBage1example1\fR, while an \fBIDENTITY\fR starts with \fBAGE\-PLUGIN\-EXAMPLE\-1\fR\. They both encode arbitrary plugin\-specific data, and are generated by the plugin\.
.P
When either is specified, \fBage\fR searches for \fBage\-plugin\-example\fR in the PATH and executes it to perform the file header encryption or decryption\. The plugin may request input from the user through \fBage\fR to complete the operation\.
.P
Plugins can be freely mixed with other plugins or natively supported keys\.
.P

.TH "AGE\-PLUGIN\-BATCHPASS" "1" "December 2025" ""
.SH "NAME"
\fBage\-plugin\-batchpass\fR \- non\-interactive passphrase encryption plugin for age(1)
.SH "SYNOPSIS"
\fBage\fR \fB\-e\fR \fB\-j\fR \fBbatchpass\fR
.br
\fBage\fR \fB\-d\fR \fB\-j\fR \fBbatchpass\fR
.br
.SH "DESCRIPTION"
\fBage\-plugin\-batchpass\fR is an age(1) plugin that enables non\-interactive passphrase\-based encryption and decryption using environment variables\.
.SH "WARNING"
This functionality is not built into the age CLI because most applications should use native keys instead of scripting passphrase\-based encryption\.
.P
Humans are notoriously bad at remembering and generating strong passphrases\. age uses scrypt to partially mitigate this, which is necessarily very slow\.
.P
If a computer will be doing the remembering anyway, you can and should use native keys instead\. There is no need to manage separate public and private keys, you encrypt directly to the private key:
.IP "" 4
.nf
$ age\-keygen \-o key\.txt
$ age \-e \-i key\.txt file\.txt > file\.txt\.age
$ age \-d \-i key\.txt file\.txt\.age > file\.txt
.fi
.IP "" 0
.P
Likewise, you can store a native identity string in an environment variable or through your CI secrets manager and use it to encrypt and decrypt files non\-interactively:
.IP "" 4
.nf
$ export AGE_SECRET=$(age\-keygen)
$ age \-e \-i <(echo "$AGE_SECRET") file\.txt > file\.txt\.age
$ age \-d \-i <(echo "$AGE_SECRET") file\.txt\.age > file\.txt
.fi
.IP "" 0
.P
The age CLI also natively supports passphrase\-encrypted identity files, so you can use that functionality to non\-interactively encrypt multiple files such that you will be able to decrypt them later by entering the same passphrase:
.IP "" 4
.nf
$ age\-keygen \-pq | age \-p \-o encrypted\-identity\.txt
Public key: age1pq1cd[\|\.\|\.\|\. 1950 more characters \|\.\|\.\|\.]
Enter passphrase (leave empty to autogenerate a secure one):
age: using autogenerated passphrase "eternal\-erase\-keen\-suffer\-fog\-exclude\-huge\-scorpion\-escape\-scrub"
$ age \-r age1pq1cd[\|\.\|\.\|\. 1950 more characters \|\.\|\.\|\.] file\.txt > file\.txt\.age
$ age \-d \-i encrypted\-identity\.txt file\.txt\.age > file\.txt
Enter passphrase for identity file "encrypted\-identity\.txt":
.fi
.IP "" 0
.P
Finally, when using this plugin care should be taken not to let the password be persisted in the shell history or leaked to other users on multi\-user systems\.
.SH "ENVIRONMENT"
.TP
\fBAGE_PASSPHRASE\fR
The passphrase to use for encryption or decryption\. Mutually exclusive with \fBAGE_PASSPHRASE_FD\fR\.
.TP
\fBAGE_PASSPHRASE_FD\fR
A file descriptor number to read the passphrase from\. Trailing newlines are stripped from the file contents\. Mutually exclusive with \fBAGE_PASSPHRASE\fR\.
.TP
\fBAGE_PASSPHRASE_WORK_FACTOR\fR
The scrypt work factor to use when encrypting\. Must be between 1 and 30\. Default is 18\. Higher values are more secure but slower\.
.TP
\fBAGE_PASSPHRASE_MAX_WORK_FACTOR\fR
The maximum scrypt work factor to accept when decrypting\. Must be between 1 and 30\. Default is 30\. Can be used to avoid very slow decryptions\.
.SH "EXAMPLES"
Encrypt a file with a passphrase:
.IP "" 4
.nf
$ AGE_PASSPHRASE=secret age \-e \-j batchpass file\.txt > file\.txt\.age
.fi
.IP "" 0
.P
Decrypt a file with a passphrase:
.IP "" 4
.nf
$ AGE_PASSPHRASE=secret age \-d \-j batchpass file\.txt\.age > file\.txt
.fi
.IP "" 0
.P
Read the passphrase from a file descriptor:
.IP "" 4
.nf
$ AGE_PASSPHRASE_FD=3 age \-e \-j batchpass file\.txt 3< passphrase\.txt > file\.txt\.age
.fi
.IP "" 0

"""Cryptographic building blocks used by the file format implementation.

Only standard Python modules and the system's general-purpose OpenSSL library
are used. Format-specific operations are implemented in the other modules.
"""
import base64
import ctypes
import ctypes.util
import hashlib
import hmac
import os


class DecodeError(ValueError):
    pass


def b64encode(data):
    return base64.b64encode(data).rstrip(b'=')


def b64decode(data, padded=False, strict=True, newlines=False):
    if isinstance(data, str):
        data = data.encode('utf-8', 'surrogateescape')
    if not newlines and (b'\r' in data or b'\n' in data):
        raise DecodeError('unexpected newline character')
    alphabet = b'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/'
    chars = []
    indices = []
    for i, c in enumerate(data):
        if newlines and c in (10, 13):
            continue
        if c in alphabet or (padded and c == 61):
            chars.append(c)
            indices.append(i)
        else:
            raise DecodeError('illegal base64 data at input byte %d' % i)
    clean = bytes(chars)
    if padded:
        pos = clean.find(b'=')
        if pos >= 0:
            n = len(clean) - pos
            valid = n in (1, 2) and len(clean) % 4 == 0 and pos % 4 in (2, 3) and clean[pos:] == b'=' * n
            if not valid:
                bad = pos
                if pos % 4 in (2, 3):
                    bad = min(pos + (4 - pos % 4), len(clean)-1)
                raise DecodeError('illegal base64 data at input byte %d' % indices[bad])
        elif len(clean) % 4:
            bad = len(clean) - len(clean) % 4
            raise DecodeError('illegal base64 data at input byte %d' % (indices[bad] if bad < len(indices) else len(data)))
        raw = clean.rstrip(b'=')
    else:
        raw = clean
        if len(raw) % 4 == 1:
            raise DecodeError('illegal base64 data at input byte %d' % (indices[len(raw)-1] if indices else 0))
    if strict and raw:
        last = alphabet.index(raw[-1])
        if len(raw) % 4 == 2 and last & 15:
            pos = len(raw) - 2
            raise DecodeError('illegal base64 data at input byte %d' % (indices[pos] if pos < len(indices) else pos))
        if len(raw) % 4 == 3 and last & 3:
            pos = len(raw) - 1
            raise DecodeError('illegal base64 data at input byte %d' % (indices[pos] if pos < len(indices) else pos))
    try:
        return base64.b64decode(raw + b'=' * (-len(raw) % 4))
    except Exception:
        raise DecodeError('illegal base64 data at input byte 0')


def hkdf(key, salt=b'', info=b'', length=32):
    prk = hmac.digest(salt, key, 'sha256')
    block = b''
    out = b''
    for i in range(1, (length + 31)//32 + 1):
        block = hmac.digest(prk, block + info + bytes([i]), 'sha256')
        out += block
    return out[:length]


def x25519(private, public=b'\x09' + b'\0'*31):
    n = int.from_bytes(private, 'little')
    n = (n & ((1 << 255) - 8)) | (1 << 254)
    p = 2**255 - 19
    x1 = int.from_bytes(public, 'little') & ((1 << 255) - 1)
    x2, z2, x3, z3, swap = 1, 0, x1, 1, 0
    for i in range(254, -1, -1):
        bit = (n >> i) & 1
        swap ^= bit
        if swap:
            x2, x3 = x3, x2
            z2, z3 = z3, z2
        swap = bit
        a = (x2 + z2) % p
        aa = a*a % p
        b = (x2 - z2) % p
        bb = b*b % p
        e = (aa - bb) % p
        c = (x3 + z3) % p
        d = (x3 - z3) % p
        da, cb = d*a % p, c*b % p
        x3, z3 = (da+cb)**2 % p, x1*(da-cb)**2 % p
        x2, z2 = aa*bb % p, e*(aa+121665*e) % p
    if swap:

"""ML-KEM-768 and its hybrid recipient framing.

Polynomial arithmetic is expressed directly over Z_3329. SHA-3 and SHAKE are
provided by hashlib. This deliberately favors a compact, auditable algorithm
rather than architecture-specific optimized transforms.
"""
import hashlib
import os
from .errors import AgeError
from .primitives import b64encode,b64decode,hkdf,x25519,seal,unseal,DecodeError

Q=3329
DOMAIN=b'age-encryption.org/v1/mlkem768x25519'

def bitreverse(n):
    return int(format(n,'07b')[::-1],2)

ZETAS=[pow(17,bitreverse(i),Q) for i in range(128)]
GAMMAS=[pow(17,2*bitreverse(i)+1,Q) for i in range(128)]


def ntt(poly):
    f=list(poly)
    length=128
    k=1
    while length>=2:
        for start in range(0,256,2*length):
            z=ZETAS[k];k+=1
            for j in range(start,start+length):
                t=z*f[j+length]%Q
                f[j+length]=(f[j]-t)%Q
                f[j]=(f[j]+t)%Q
        length//=2
    return f


def invntt(poly):
    f=list(poly)
    k=127
    length=2
    while length<=128:
        for start in range(0,256,2*length):
            z=ZETAS[k];k-=1
            for j in range(start,start+length):
                t=f[j]
                f[j]=(t+f[j+length])%Q
                f[j+length]=z*(f[j+length]-t)%Q
        length*=2
    return [x*3303%Q for x in f]


def mul(a,b):
    c=[0]*256
    for i in range(128):
        j=2*i
        c[j]=(a[j]*b[j]+GAMMAS[i]*a[j+1]*b[j+1])%Q
        c[j+1]=(a[j]*b[j+1]+a[j+1]*b[j])%Q
    return c


def add(a,b):
    return [(x+y)%Q for x,y in zip(a,b)]


def dot(a,b):
    result=[0]*256
    for x,y in zip(a,b):
        result=add(result,mul(x,y))
    return result


def sample_ntt(seed):

"""P-256 recipient encodings, ECDH, and tagged recipient framing."""
import hashlib
import os
from .errors import AgeError
from .primitives import b64encode,seal
from .hpke import schedule,labeled_extract,labeled_expand

P=2**256-2**224+2**192+2**96-1
N=int('ffffffff00000000ffffffffffffffffbce6faada7179e84f3b9cac2fc632551',16)
B=int('5ac635d8aa3a93e7b3ebbd55769886bc651d06b0cc53b0f63bce3c3e27d2604b',16)
G=(int('6b17d1f2e12c4247f8bce6e563a440f277037d812deb33a0f4a13945d898c296',16),int('4fe342e2fe1a7f9b8ee7eb4a7c0f9e162bce33576b315ececbb6406837bf51f5',16))


def point_add(a,b):
    if a is None:return b
    if b is None:return a
    x,y=a;u,v=b
    if x==u:
        if (y+v)%P==0:return None
        slope=(3*x*x-3)*pow(2*y,P-2,P)%P
    else:
        slope=(v-y)*pow(u-x,P-2,P)%P
    xx=(slope*slope-x-u)%P
    return xx,(slope*(x-xx)-y)%P


def point_mul(k,p):
    acc=None
    while k:
        if k&1:acc=point_add(acc,p)
        p=point_add(p,p)
        k>>=1
    return acc


def decode_point(data):
    if len(data)==33 and data[0] in (2,3):
        x=int.from_bytes(data[1:],'big')
        y=pow((x*x*x-3*x+B)%P,(P+1)//4,P)
        if y%2!=data[0]%2:y=P-y
    elif len(data)==65 and data[0]==4:
        x=int.from_bytes(data[1:33],'big');y=int.from_bytes(data[33:],'big')
    else:
        raise AgeError('invalid P256 point encoding')
    if x>=P or y>=P or (y*y-x*x*x+3*x-B)%P:
        raise AgeError('invalid P256 point encoding')
    return x,y


def encode_point(p,compressed=False):
    x,y=p
    if compressed:return bytes([2+y%2])+x.to_bytes(32,'big')
    return b'\4'+x.to_bytes(32,'big')+y.to_bytes(32,'big')


class TagKey:
    pq=False
    def __init__(self,public):
        try:
            self.point=decode_point(public)
        except AgeError as e:
            raise AgeError('invalid tag recipient public key: '+str(e))
        self.public=encode_point(self.point)

    def wrap(self,filekey):
        scalar=int.from_bytes(os.urandom(32),'big')%(N-1)+1
        ep=encode_point(point_mul(scalar,G))

        shared=labeled_expand(prk,suite,b'shared_secret',ep+self.public,32)

        body=seal(key,filekey,nonce)
        tag=hashlib.sha256(b'age-encryption.org/tag'+self.public+ep+body).digest()[:4]

import hashlib
import os
from .errors import AgeError
from .primitives import b64encode,seal
from .hpke import schedule,labeled_extract,labeled_expand

P=2**256-2**224+2**192+2**96-1
N=int('ffffffff00000000ffffffffffffffffbce6faada7179e84f3b9cac2fc632551',16)
B=int('5ac635d8aa3a93e7b3ebbd55769886bc651d06b0cc53b0f63bce3c3e27d2604b',16)
G=(int('6b17d1f2e12c4247f8bce6e563a440f277037d812deb33a0f4a13945d898c296',16),int('4fe342e2fe1a7f9b8ee7eb4a7c0f9e162bce33576b315ececbb6406837bf51f5',16))


def point_add(a,b):
    if a is None:return b
    if b is None:return a
    x,y=a;u,v=b
    if x==u:
        if (y+v)%P==0:return None
        slope=(3*x*x-3)*pow(2*y,P-2,P)%P
    else:
        slope=(v-y)*pow(u-x,P-2,P)%P
    xx=(slope*slope-x-u)%P
    return xx,(slope*(x-xx)-y)%P


def point_mul(k,p):
    acc=None
    while k:
        if k&1:acc=point_add(acc,p)
        p=point_add(p,p)
        k>>=1
    return acc


def decode_point(data):
    if len(data)==33 and data[0] in (2,3):
        x=int.from_bytes(data[1:],'big')
        y=pow((x*x*x-3*x+B)%P,(P+1)//4,P)
        if y%2!=data[0]%2:y=P-y
    elif len(data)==65 and data[0]==4:
        x=int.from_bytes(data[1:33],'big');y=int.from_bytes(data[33:],'big')
    else:
        raise AgeError('invalid P256 point encoding')
    if x>=P or y>=P or (y*y-x*x*x+3*x-B)%P:
        raise AgeError('invalid P256 point encoding')
    return x,y


def encode_point(p,compressed=False):
    x,y=p
    if compressed:return bytes([2+y%2])+x.to_bytes(32,'big')
    return b'\4'+x.to_bytes(32,'big')+y.to_bytes(32,'big')


class TagKey:
    pq=False
    def __init__(self,public):
        try:
            self.point=decode_point(public)
        except AgeError as e:
            raise AgeError('invalid tag recipient public key: '+str(e))
        self.public=encode_point(self.point)

    def wrap(self,filekey):
        scalar=int.from_bytes(os.urandom(32),'big')%(N-1)+1
        ep=encode_point(point_mul(scalar,G))
        shared=point_mul(scalar,self.point)[0].to_bytes(32,'big')
        suite=b'KEM\0\x10'
        prk=labeled_extract(b'',suite,b'eae_prk',shared)
        shared=labeled_expand(prk,suite,b'shared_secret',ep+self.public,32)
        key,nonce=schedule(shared,0x10,b'age-encryption.org/p256tag')
        body=seal(key,filekey,nonce)
        tag=hashlib.sha256(b'age-encryption.org/tag'+self.public+ep+body).digest()[:4]
        return [('p256tag',[b64encode(tag).decode(),b64encode(ep).decode()],body)]


class TagPQKey:
    pq=True
    def __init__(self,public):

        body=seal(key,filekey,nonce)
        tag=hashlib.sha256(b'age-encryption.org/tag'+self.public+enc+body).digest()[:4]

def decrypt_pem_block(cipher,iv,password,ciphertext):
    import hashlib
    methods={'AES-128-CBC':(16,'EVP_aes_128_cbc'),'AES-192-CBC':(24,'EVP_aes_192_cbc'),'AES-256-CBC':(32,'EVP_aes_256_cbc'),'DES-EDE3-CBC':(24,'EVP_des_ede3_cbc'),'DES-CBC':(8,'EVP_des_cbc')}
    if cipher not in methods:
        raise AgeError('x509: unknown encryption mode')
    keylen,name=methods[cipher]
    key=b''
    previous=b''
    while len(key)<keylen:
        previous=hashlib.md5(previous+password+iv[:8]).digest()
        key+=previous
    key=key[:keylen]
    lib=crypto();ptr=ctypes.c_void_p
    getcipher=getattr(lib,name)
    getcipher.argtypes=[];getcipher.restype=ptr
    ctx=lib.EVP_CIPHER_CTX_new()
    try:
        if not lib.EVP_DecryptInit_ex(ctx,getcipher(),None,key,iv):
            raise AgeError('x509: unknown encryption mode')
        out=ctypes.create_string_buffer(len(ciphertext)+32)
        n=ctypes.c_int()
        if not lib.EVP_DecryptUpdate(ctx,out,ctypes.byref(n),ciphertext,len(ciphertext)):
            raise AgeError('x509: decryption password incorrect')
        size=n.value
        if not lib.EVP_DecryptFinal_ex(ctx,ctypes.byref(out,size),ctypes.byref(n)):
            raise AgeError('x509: decryption password incorrect')
        return out.raw[:size+n.value]
    finally:
        lib.EVP_CIPHER_CTX_free(ctx)

def decrypt_pem_block(cipher,iv,password,ciphertext):
    import hashlib
    methods={'AES-128-CBC':(16,'EVP_aes_128_cbc'),'AES-192-CBC':(24,'EVP_aes_192_cbc'),'AES-256-CBC':(32,'EVP_aes_256_cbc'),'DES-EDE3-CBC':(24,'EVP_des_ede3_cbc'),'DES-CBC':(8,'EVP_des_cbc')}
    if cipher not in methods:
        raise AgeError('x509: unknown encryption mode')
    keylen,name=methods[cipher]
    key=b''
    previous=b''
    while len(key)<keylen:
        previous=hashlib.md5(previous+password+iv[:8]).digest()
        key+=previous
    key=key[:keylen]
    lib=crypto();ptr=ctypes.c_void_p
    getcipher=getattr(lib,name)
    getcipher.argtypes=[];getcipher.restype=ptr
    ctx=lib.EVP_CIPHER_CTX_new()
    try:
        if not lib.EVP_DecryptInit_ex(ctx,getcipher(),None,key,iv):
            raise AgeError('x509: unknown encryption mode')
        out=ctypes.create_string_buffer(len(ciphertext)+32)
        n=ctypes.c_int()
        if not lib.EVP_DecryptUpdate(ctx,out,ctypes.byref(n),ciphertext,len(ciphertext)):
            raise AgeError('x509: decryption password incorrect')
        size=n.value
        if not lib.EVP_DecryptFinal_ex(ctx,ctypes.byref(out,size),ctypes.byref(n)):
            raise AgeError('x509: decryption password incorrect')
        return out.raw[:size+n.value]
    finally:
        lib.EVP_CIPHER_CTX_free(ctx)

class Primitives(unittest.TestCase):

        secret = 'AGE-SECRET-KEY-1N9JEPW6DWJ0ZQUDX63F5A03GX8QUW7PXDE39N8UYF82VZ9PC8UFS3M7XA9'
        public = 'age1lvyvwawkr0mcnnnncaghunadrqkmuf9e6507x9y920xxpp866cnql7dp2z'
        _, raw = bech_decode(secret)
        self.assertEqual(bech_encode('age',x25519(raw)),public)
        self.assertEqual(bech_encode('AGE-SECRET-KEY-',raw),secret)

        message=b'authenticated bytes\0\xff'
        encrypted=seal(key,message)
        self.assertEqual(unseal(key,encrypted),message)
        self.assertIsNone(unseal(key,encrypted[:-1]+bytes([encrypted[-1]^1])))

        self.assertEqual(invntt(ntt(polynomial)),polynomial)
        kem=MLKEM(seed=bytes(range(64)))
        public=MLKEM(public=kem.public)
        ciphertext,key=public.encapsulate()
        self.assertEqual(len(ciphertext),1088)
        self.assertEqual(kem.decapsulate(ciphertext),key)

        self.assertNotEqual(kem.decapsulate(damaged),key)

    def setUp(self):

        self.secret=bytes(range(32))
        self.key=self.directory/'identity.txt'
        self.key.write_text('# test identity\n'+bech_encode('AGE-SECRET-KEY-',self.secret)+'\n')
        self.public=bech_encode('age',x25519(self.secret))

    def tearDown(self):
        self.temp.cleanup()

    def test_help_and_version(self):
        result=command('--version')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,0)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout,b'v0.0.0-20260611192840-f11ca54177da\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stderr,b'')
        result=command('--help')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,0)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout,b'')
        self.assertTrue(result.stderr.startswith(b'Usage:\n    age '))
        self.assertEqual(command().returncode,1)

    def test_go_style_flag_parsing(self):
        result=command('-ed')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,2)
        self.assertTrue(result.stderr.startswith(b'flag provided but not defined: -ed\nUsage:'))
        result=command('-r')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,2)
        self.assertTrue(result.stderr.startswith(b'flag needs an argument: -r\nUsage:'))
        result=command('-d','-a')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,1)
        self.assertIn(b'armored files are detected automatically',result.stderr)
        self.assertTrue(result.stderr.endswith(REPORT))

    def test_duplicate_warning_is_once(self):
        result=command('-r','bad','-r','bad','-r','bad')
        self.assertEqual(result.stderr.count(b'age: warning: duplicate recipient'),1)
        self.assertIn(b'unknown recipient type: "bad"',result.stderr)

    def test_identity_requires_explicit_mode(self):
        result=command('-i',str(self.key))
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,1)
        self.assertIn(b'did you forget to specify -d/--decrypt?',result.stderr)

    def test_classic_stream_boundaries(self):
        for size in [0,1,65535,65536,65537,131072]:
            with self.subTest(size=size):
                message=(bytes(range(256))*((size+255)//256))[:size]
                result=command('-r',self.public,data=message)
                self.assertEqual(result.returncode,0,result.stderr)
                self.assertEqual(len(result.stdout),168+16+size+16*max(1,(size+65535)//65536))
                restored=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),data=result.stdout)
                self.assertEqual(restored.returncode,0,restored.stderr)
                self.assertEqual(restored.stdout,message)

    def test_armored_stream(self):
        result=command('-a','-e','-i',str(self.key),data=b'armor\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,0,result.stderr)
        lines=result.stdout.splitlines()
        self.assertEqual(lines[0],ARMOR_START)
        self.assertEqual(lines[-1],ARMOR_END)
        self.assertTrue(all(len(line)==64 for line in lines[1:-2]))
        binary=base64.b64decode(b''.join(lines[1:-1]))
        self.assertTrue(binary.startswith(INTRO))
        restored=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),data=b'\n'+result.stdout.replace(b'\n',b'\r\n'))
        self.assertEqual(restored.stdout,b'armor\n')
        self.assertEqual(restored.returncode,0,restored.stderr)

    def test_post_quantum_round_trip(self):
        self.key.write_text(bech_encode('AGE-SECRET-KEY-PQ-',self.secret)+'\n')
        message=b'hybrid recipients\0'+bytes(range(256))
        result=command('-e','-i',str(self.key),data=message)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,0,result.stderr)
        self.assertTrue(result.stdout.startswith(INTRO+b'-> mlkem768x25519 '))
        restored=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),data=result.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(restored.returncode,0,restored.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(restored.stdout,message)
        result=command('-e','-i',str(self.key),'-r',self.public)
        self.assertIn(b"can't mix post-quantum and classic recipients",result.stderr)

    def test_authentication_and_partial_output(self):
        key=os.urandom(16)
        recipient=XKey(secret=self.secret)
        header=make_header(recipient.wrap(key),key)
        encrypted=header+encrypt_payload(key,b'a'*65537)
        cut=len(header)+16+65552
        result=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),data=encrypted[:cut])
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,1)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout,b'a'*65536)
        self.assertIn(b'age: error: unexpected EOF\n',result.stderr)
        result=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),data=encrypted[:-1])
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout,b'a'*65536)
        self.assertIn(b'last chunk is empty',result.stderr)
        damaged=bytearray(encrypted)
        damaged[len(header)+20]^=1
        result=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),data=bytes(damaged))
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,1)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout,b'')

    def test_output_is_lazy_until_nonce(self):
        out=self.directory/'output'
        out.write_bytes(b'existing')
        result=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),'-o',str(out),data=b'not encrypted')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,1)
        self.assertEqual(out.read_bytes(),b'existing')

    def test_recipient_list_comments(self):
        recipients=self.directory/'recipients'
        recipients.write_text('# list\n\n'+self.public+'\r\n')
        result=command('-R',str(recipients),data=b'recipients')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,0,result.stderr)
        result=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),data=result.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout,b'recipients')
        recipients.write_text('  # not a comment\n')
        result=command('-R',str(recipients))
        self.assertIn(b'malformed recipient at line 1',result.stderr)

    def test_missing_plugin(self):
        result=command('-e','-j','test-plugin-not-installed')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,1)
        self.assertIn(b'plugin not found: exec: "age-plugin-test-plugin-not-installed"',result.stderr)
        self.assertIn(b'you might want to install',result.stderr)


if __name__=='__main__':
    unittest.main()

        self.assertEqual(result.stdout,b'v0.0.0-20260611192840-f11ca54177da\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.stderr,b'')
        result=command('--help')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,0)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout,b'')
        self.assertTrue(result.stderr.startswith(b'Usage:\n    age '))
        self.assertEqual(command().returncode,1)

    def test_go_style_flag_parsing(self):
        result=command('-ed')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,2)
        self.assertTrue(result.stderr.startswith(b'flag provided but not defined: -ed\nUsage:'))
        result=command('-r')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,2)
        self.assertTrue(result.stderr.startswith(b'flag needs an argument: -r\nUsage:'))
        result=command('-d','-a')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,1)
        self.assertIn(b'armored files are detected automatically',result.stderr)
        self.assertTrue(result.stderr.endswith(REPORT))

    def test_duplicate_warning_is_once(self):
        result=command('-r','bad','-r','bad','-r','bad')
        self.assertEqual(result.stderr.count(b'age: warning: duplicate recipient'),1)
        self.assertIn(b'unknown recipient type: "bad"',result.stderr)

    def test_identity_requires_explicit_mode(self):
        result=command('-i',str(self.key))
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,1)
        self.assertIn(b'did you forget to specify -d/--decrypt?',result.stderr)

    def test_classic_stream_boundaries(self):
        for size in [0,1,65535,65536,65537,131072]:
            with self.subTest(size=size):
                message=(bytes(range(256))*((size+255)//256))[:size]
                result=command('-r',self.public,data=message)
                self.assertEqual(result.returncode,0,result.stderr)
                self.assertEqual(len(result.stdout),168+16+size+16*max(1,(size+65535)//65536))
                restored=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),data=result.stdout)
                self.assertEqual(restored.returncode,0,restored.stderr)
                self.assertEqual(restored.stdout,message)

    def test_armored_stream(self):
        result=command('-a','-e','-i',str(self.key),data=b'armor\n')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,0,result.stderr)
        lines=result.stdout.splitlines()
        self.assertEqual(lines[0],ARMOR_START)
        self.assertEqual(lines[-1],ARMOR_END)
        self.assertTrue(all(len(line)==64 for line in lines[1:-2]))
        binary=base64.b64decode(b''.join(lines[1:-1]))
        self.assertTrue(binary.startswith(INTRO))
        restored=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),data=b'\n'+result.stdout.replace(b'\n',b'\r\n'))
        self.assertEqual(restored.stdout,b'armor\n')
        self.assertEqual(restored.returncode,0,restored.stderr)

    def test_post_quantum_round_trip(self):
        self.key.write_text(bech_encode('AGE-SECRET-KEY-PQ-',self.secret)+'\n')
        message=b'hybrid recipients\0'+bytes(range(256))
        result=command('-e','-i',str(self.key),data=message)
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,0,result.stderr)
        self.assertTrue(result.stdout.startswith(INTRO+b'-> mlkem768x25519 '))
        restored=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),data=result.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(restored.returncode,0,restored.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(restored.stdout,message)
        result=command('-e','-i',str(self.key),'-r',self.public)
        self.assertIn(b"can't mix post-quantum and classic recipients",result.stderr)

    def test_authentication_and_partial_output(self):
        key=os.urandom(16)
        recipient=XKey(secret=self.secret)
        header=make_header(recipient.wrap(key),key)
        encrypted=header+encrypt_payload(key,b'a'*65537)
        cut=len(header)+16+65552
        result=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),data=encrypted[:cut])
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,1)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout,b'a'*65536)
        self.assertIn(b'age: error: unexpected EOF\n',result.stderr)
        result=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),data=encrypted[:-1])
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout,b'a'*65536)
        self.assertIn(b'last chunk is empty',result.stderr)
        damaged=bytearray(encrypted)
        damaged[len(header)+20]^=1
        result=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),data=bytes(damaged))
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,1)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout,b'')

    def test_output_is_lazy_until_nonce(self):
        out=self.directory/'output'
        out.write_bytes(b'existing')
        result=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),'-o',str(out),data=b'not encrypted')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,1)
        self.assertEqual(out.read_bytes(),b'existing')

    def test_recipient_list_comments(self):
        recipients=self.directory/'recipients'
        recipients.write_text('# list\n\n'+self.public+'\r\n')
        result=command('-R',str(recipients),data=b'recipients')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,0,result.stderr)
        result=command('-d','-i',str(self.key),data=result.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout,b'recipients')
        recipients.write_text('  # not a comment\n')
        result=command('-R',str(recipients))
        self.assertIn(b'malformed recipient at line 1',result.stderr)

    def test_missing_plugin(self):
        result=command('-e','-j','test-plugin-not-installed')
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode,1)
        self.assertIn(b'plugin not found: exec: "age-plugin-test-plugin-not-installed"',result.stderr)
        self.assertIn(b'you might want to install',result.stderr)


if __name__=='__main__':
    unittest.main()
